title: Gematria

scenario.title: The simplest checksum there is
scenario.body: Adding up character codes is a checksum: a number that changes when the text changes (most of the time). These tests pin down what it can't tell apart (listen and silent get the same number). They also catch two quiet mistakes: the book throws away accented letters, so café scores the same as caf, and a lone "--" gets the number 0.

character.name: Abacus Annie
character.role: a squirrel who counts letters like nuts

tagline: Every letter has a secret number inside the computer (A is 65, a is 97). Annie adds them up, so every word gets its own number. Can you find two words with the same one?

brain_blurbs.book: Keeps only A to Z and 0 to 9, and adds them up.
brain_blurbs.real: Counts é as e, and skips bits that aren't words at all.

rules.test_usage: Explains herself when you ask for help
rules.test_fox: Gives every word of the fox sentence its number
rules.test_spiders: Ignores the ' in "Don't" and keeps the lines
rules.test_sonnet: Counts a whole sonnet, blank line and all
rules.test_anagrams_collide: "listen" and "silent" get the same number (same letters, mixed up!)
rules.test_lone_punctuation_is_not_a_word: A lone "--" or 🙂 isn't a word, so it gets no number
rules.test_blank_lines_stay: A blank line stays a blank line
